clue.text: Six gunners attempt to bring down a Spitfire

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
to have a go is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: Anti-aircraft gunners are trying to shoot down a wartime fighter plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spitfire looks like the RAF fighter, but here it is a fiery-tempered woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A spitfire is a hot-tempered, quarrelsome woman, which is what a virago is.

clue.text: Writer on farm-butter is not released

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next, so the first comes before the second

parts.note: a pen is the thing a writer writes with
a tup is a ram, the farm animal that butts

explanation.surface: Someone who writes about farm butter has a story that never gets released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'farm-butter' reads as dairy butter, but it is something on a farm that butts: a ram, TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings that are held in and kept bottled up are not let out or released.

clue.text: One of the last eight quits flat in rear, unexpectedly

indicators.note: something arranged unexpectedly comes out in a surprising order, so these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tournament player leaves a flat at the back without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' signals an anagram of QUITS FLAT IN REAR, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The last eight in a knockout tournament are those who reach the round before the semi-finals.

clue.text: Town-criers to call me before noon

indicators.note: one piece placed before the next in the down light

parts.note: to bell is an old word for to call out or bellow

explanation.surface: Town-criers summon the speaker before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Town-criers rang a hand bell to call attention before reading out news.

clue.text: Footballers who are modern keep together

parts.note: new means modern
a keep is the stronghold of a castle, so stands for the castle itself
united means joined together

explanation.surface: Modern players who stick together.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWCASTLE UNITED is an English Premier League football club. 'keep' is a noun here, the fortified tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The team's players are a set of footballers.

clue.text: One helps to steer fish over water

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a cod is a sea fish
a river is a body of water

explanation.surface: Someone guides a fish across a stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-driver shares the driving and navigating in rallies, helping steer the car.

clue.text: Break up, divorce and vanish!

definitions.meaning: to break up into parts or fragments
to end a marriage or partnership legally

explanation.surface: An angry command to split, divorce and disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissolving a solid breaks it up, dissolving a marriage ends it, and something dissolving fades into nothing.

clue.text: Nice changes in reliable, cushy job

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed inside the other word

parts.note: sure means reliable or certain

indicators.note: the word nice changes its letter order, so it is scrambled

explanation.surface: A job in Nice that changes into a dependable, easy number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city, but it is just fodder: 'changes' makes INEC, which goes 'in' SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post requiring little or no work.

clue.text: Tempo in Beethoven's unfinished symphony is stimulating

indicators.note: the tempo letter goes inside the shortened symphony name
unfinished means the symphony's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's third symphony
T is a standard abbreviation for tempo in music

explanation.surface: The pace of an incomplete Beethoven symphony is exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Third Symphony is the Eroica; 'unfinished' cuts its last letter to leave EROIC, and T goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erotic arouses desire, so it is sexually stimulating.

clue.text: Owl, unusually, at ground-level

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of the bird's name are set in an odd order

explanation.surface: An owl, unusually, is found down on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'Ow' is an OCR slip for 'Owl', whose letters rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something near the floor or the earth is not high up but down beneath.

clue.text: Rural priest takes on a novice

parts.note: a pastor is a minister or priest in charge of a congregation
L is a learner, the novice driver's plate

explanation.surface: A country vicar takes a beginner under his wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes the countryside and country life.

clue.text: Pat is anxious, starting school

parts.note: someone who cares is worried or anxious

indicators.note: starting means only the first letter of school is taken

explanation.surface: Pat is nervous about starting school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' reads as a child's name, but it is the verb, to stroke gently.
explanation.definitionFit: To pat someone is to touch them lightly and affectionately, a gentle stroke.

clue.text: School play Pa left, all ends up

parts.note: a comprehensive is a British state secondary school taking all abilities

indicators.note: Pa having left means those letters are removed from the word play

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dad walks out of the school play and everything is turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school. 'all ends up' is the idiom 'all ends up', meaning thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone all ends up is to defeat them completely and thoroughly.

clue.text: Drive in reverse-hurt results

indicators.note: in reverse means the synonym for drive is written backwards

parts.note: to ram is to drive or force something in

explanation.surface: Driving backwards causes damage.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or damage it.

clue.text: Check truth about somebody starting to write poetry

indicators.note: about means the other word is wrapped around the letter

parts.note: to verify is to check that something is true

indicators.note: starting means only the opening letter of somebody is used

explanation.surface: Someone checks the facts before beginning to compose verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To versify is to turn something into verse, composing poems.

clue.text: Importance of cardinal's address?

definitions.meaning: a cardinal is formally addressed as Your ...

explanation.surface: How grand is a cardinal when you speak to him?
explanation.definitionFit: Distinction and fame are high standing, and 'Your Eminence' is the formal style for a cardinal.

clue.text: Plane may score, used clumsily

indicators.note: letters used clumsily are thrown into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: An aircraft might register a hit if flown badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a maple, and in North America the name is used for the plane tree.

clue.text: Possibly pursed lips at first and drank noisily

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be arranged another way
at first means only the opening letter of lips is taken

explanation.surface: With lips pursed, someone noisily sips a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' scrambles PURSED together with L, the first letter of 'lips'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slurping is sucking a drink up with a loud noise.

clue.text: Get a letter from Greece after hip replacement

indicators.note: a replacement here means the letters of hip are moved into new positions

explanation.surface: Fetching a letter from Greece after a hip operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip replacement' reads as surgery, but 'replacement' only rearranges HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Bread for the beak?

parts.note: bread is slang for money, and a beak is British slang for a magistrate, so this asks what pays a salaried magistrate

explanation.surface: Something for a bird to peck at.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests feeding birds; in British slang 'beak' is a magistrate and 'bread' is money.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular salary, especially for a clergyman or magistrate.

clue.text: Wrong idea of motorway's assembly

parts.note: M is a motorway, as in the M1, and the 's stands for is
construction is the act of assembling or building

explanation.surface: A false impression of how the motorway was built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motorway's' gives M plus IS, the 's read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A misconstruction is a misreading or misunderstanding, a mistaken interpretation.

clue.text: How Caesar addressed Brutus, with possibly less struggle

parts.note: Caesar's dying words in Shakespeare are 'Et tu, Brute?', tu being the Latin for you

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of less could be rearranged

explanation.surface: Caesar's words to Brutus, with less fighting than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous scuffle or fight.

clue.text: Stupid to put ring on a natural swimmer!

parts.note: O is a ring, from its round shape
a fish swims by nature

explanation.surface: It's daft to put a ring on a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Oafish means clumsy and dull-witted, like a lout.

clue.text: Section of redder Malpighian layer of skin

indicators.note: a section of these words is taken, the run of letters lying across them

explanation.surface: A slice of the reddened Malpighian layer of the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Malpighian layer is a real layer of the skin, so the surface reads as biology; 'Maphigian' is an OCR slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Dermal is the adjective relating to the dermis, the skin.

clue.text: Some Henley events abandoned, mates!

parts.note: Henley Royal Regatta is a British rowing event, and pairs are two-oared boat races
an event called off is abandoned

explanation.surface: Some races at the Henley regatta are cancelled, friends!
explanation.walkthrough: 'mates' looks like a friendly greeting, but it is a verb: to couple up.
explanation.definitionFit: To pair off is to couple up, as animals do when they mate.

clue.text: Girl's best friend in classic effect?

indicators.note: in means the answer lies inside these words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A girl's best friend shows its effect in a classic way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds are a girl's best friend', and ice is slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is slang for diamonds, which the song calls a girl's best friend.

clue.text: Looks down on grain in ship

indicators.note: the grain goes in, held by the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
corn is a grain crop

explanation.surface: A sailor sneers at the grain in the hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn someone is to regard them with contempt, as beneath you.

clue.text: Unnecessary IOW features, facing south

indicators.note: facing means set beside the first piece, at its end

parts.note: the Needles are chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight (IOW), an island off England's south coast

explanation.surface: The Needles on the Isle of Wight face south, which hardly needs saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off England's south coast; the Needles are its famous chalk rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needless serves no purpose and could be done without.
